logs: panel (max: finders opus/high, verifier opus/high): sweep + 5 scalpel(s) against base @ 3214b61696 (HEAD 7dc1bd78f4)

panel verdict: incorrect — confirmed: Keep a fence glued to a mark tag from swallowing the rest of the block; Skip recovery's settle when the process exits during the journal read; Bring directory listings under the post-open identity check

findings.title: Keep a fence glued to a mark tag from swallowing the rest of the block
findings.comment:
I reproduced this against the head parser with a temporary script, which I removed afterwards; the working tree is clean.

- `parse('<to-human>Run this:\n```bash\nnpm test\n```</to-human>\n<need-input>Go?</need-input>')` returns a single `plain` part.
- The same text with `</to-human>` on its own line parses correctly into to-human, plain and need-input parts.
- `'<to-human>```bash\nnpm test\n```\n</to-human>\n<need-input>Go?</need-input>'` also returns a single plain part.

The cause is in `codeRegions`. `FENCE_CLOSE` (to-human-parser.ts:20) requires only whitespace after the fence run, and `FENCE_OPEN` needs the fence at the start of the line. A glued closing tag therefore leaves the fence open to the end of the text, and in the opening-tag case the later bare ``` line opens a fence that runs to the end. Every later tag is filtered out as code.

The CommonMark closing rule was a design choice (P2-C doc line 698). Even so, the contract (contract.ts:36) only says to keep marks out of code blocks. It never tells the model to put tags on their own lines. A plausible formatting variant therefore silently drops a need-input question and the mark structure of the whole block, which grammar 1 handled. That regression is P2.

findings.title: Skip recovery's settle when the process exits during the journal read
findings.comment:
I traced this through the code and it holds. In queue.ts:117-145, `recover()` now awaits `deps.unsettled()` (prompt-history.ts `unsettledPrompts`, which walks earlier launches' journals and folds them) before it sets `this.loaded = true`. It is called from session.ts:706, after `handshakeDone = true`.

If the engine exits during that await, `handleExit` (session.ts:1094) calls `queue.onProcessExited`. That method returns at queue.ts:557 because `!this.loaded`. The exit row is then written and `journalClosed = true` is set (session.ts:1108-1109). When `recover()` resumes, `settleAfterExit()` calls `transition('abandon'|'retire'|'uncertain')`, and the RECOVERED_ACTION row is journaled after it. Each of these goes through `journal()` → `deps.meta` → `record()`, which throws `JournalClosed` (session.ts:573). The error is only logged (queue.ts:709-715). `persist()` still saves the settled state: `released` entries are dropped, `submitting` entries become queued with `uncertain: true`, and steers are cleared.

The next launch's walk does re-fold the steers, because this launch has no `recovered` row (prompt-history.ts:66-80). The `retire` and `uncertain` rows for the entries are lost for good, because the state file no longer holds those entries in their old state. P2-C introduced these rows in this diff, so this is new exposure, not pre-existing.

The window opens only when an exit lands during startup recovery, so P3 is right.

findings.title: Bring directory listings under the post-open identity check
findings.comment:
The mechanism is real. `list()` (manifest.ts:212-219) calls `readdir(found.real)` on a path that `find()` confined by realpath earlier, with no check afterwards. The new `sameFile` check (L136) covers only `read()`'s file descriptor. If an ancestor directory is swapped for a link between `find` and `readdir`, the reader lists an outside directory. Each name then goes back through `find()`, where `label = relative(anchor.real, lexical)` carries the outside name into a problem string such as `agents/<name>: outside the plugin`. That breaks the header's claim that a link may not leave the anchor.

The practical impact is close to nil, which keeps this at P3 and tracker-worthy rather than blocking:
- Only names leak, never contents.
- They reach the same user's UI.
- The racer must be a same-user process. Such a process could already write arbitrary names into the plugin directory itself.

The P2-F plan's L136 scope (2026-10-09-p2-f-finish.md:101, Decision Log 20) was file reads after open. Directory listings were simply not addressed, so this is a gap in L136's reach, not a deliberate exclusion.

The queue's transitions and `session.promptHistory`: exactly once across crash, giveback, withdraw and promote, the recovery marker.
